correctness.rationale: The kernel K=1+cos(y−x) has only Fourier modes 0,±1, hence the nonlinear Banach map has exact rank-three image E=span{1,cos,sin}. Direct independent Laurent-Fourier integration reproduces the displayed quadratic map. Independent SymPy substitution confirms a(t)=5t/N, b(t)=5t²/N, λ=N/D (N=1−5t²+16t³, D=1−4t−t²+8t³) and det(A+I)=Q/D², Q=384t⁶−44t⁵−447t⁴+122t³+88t²−34t+3. The real isolated root lies in (166763953195/10¹²,166763953197/10¹²); complementary multipliers are approximately −0.17979 and −0.50161. Independently reconstructing the left/right eigendirections, the bilinear Hessian and h=−(A−I)⁻¹ B(v,v) gives ν'=−0.96973278 and c=−19.18617853, consistent with source exact-rational enclosures (−0.98,−0.96), (−19.2,−19.1). Both signs negative imply a supercritical stable flip by the standard smooth flip theorem; finite rank ensures arbitrary C(T) perturbations enter E after one iteration. The full profile is biologically positive, with max κu in (0.74,0.75). The claim is local only; no infinite-rank Poisson-kernel result follows.

value.rationale: The nonnegative three-mode cosine kernel is the simplest nonconstant convolution kernel with exact Fourier closure, not an ad hoc Galerkin truncation. A locally attracting patterned positive period-two branch with an explicit algebraic threshold and verified normal-form sign is a reusable rigorous full-function-space benchmark for spatial dynamics, even without a global attractor theorem.
residual_risks: The example is specialized to a deliberately finite-rank dispersal kernel; general Poisson-kernel models are not settled.

final_claim: A positive cosine-kernel spatial population map has an algebraic nonconstant fixed-profile flip at λ*=2.73248006589…, producing a locally attracting positive patterned period-two branch in C(T), for precisely the specified kernel and carrying capacity.
